newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Cent. European armies end emergency staff exercise.
newsitem.headline: Cent. European armies end emergency staff exercise.

text.p: The general staffs of six central European countries, some tipped for early NATO membership, on Friday ended a staff exercise on cooperation in emergency humanitarian situations and disasters.
Taking part were the military staffs of Austria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia.

The Czechs, Poles and Hungarians are tipped to be the first to be invited to join NATO when the alliance meets for its summit in Madrid next month. Slovakia is very unlikely to be among the first new members.
But the chiefs of staff of all the participating countries agreed that NATO membership would not become an obstacle for further cooperation of the military in central Europe.

"This region will remain the same even if Slovakia is not a part of NATO," Slovak chief of staff General Jozef Tuchyna, told a news conference. "Crises can occur under all situations creating the need for cooperation in achieving peace and security in the region."

The exercise, Hexagrant 1997, concentrated on cooperation to deal with emergencies in one or more countries, including nuclear hazards and natural catastrophes, General Karl Majcen, Chief of the Austrian General Staff, said.
The next exercise will be organised by the Czechs in 1999.
